# Statement ledger

This ledger maps labels of the manuscript on the second moment of the
Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model with Gaussian noise fractional in time
to the Lean declarations in this package. Labels and TeX line numbers refer to
the manuscript revision a284420, and labels are written exactly as in its
LaTeX source (for example `P:clock-copy-obstruction`). The ledger was written
and reviewed at the earlier revisions cf979d6, 669ccc9, ba01d98, 3920258 and
975feb3. Revision a284420 makes two mathematical edits that the ledger
follows. (1) In `notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` it adds Lemma
`L:spatial-fourier-bound` (lines 101-164, display `E:spatial-fourier-bound`),
the deterministic bound `A_sp(g) <= 2^(1+alpha) R_alpha b^(alpha/2)` that
`SpatialFourierBound` already proved, and the proof of
`P:spatial-smooth-ratio` (same label and statement) now derives `R_0 < inf`
from it, independently of the finiteness of `S_1^pos`, which it keeps only
for the score inequality. (2) In the main file, `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`
replaces its smoothing and truncation sentence by the multiplier comparison
`E:damped-multiplier-comparison` (a measurable multiplier `m` in `[0,1]`,
nested measurable Laplace domains, positivity after time integration,
scaling asserted only for the original covariance) and its proof by the
corresponding argument. The other changes since 975feb3 are prose and front
matter (title, abstract, preface, a theory-outlook chapter, the reader
edition, Appendices F and G, the list of notation moved to the back).
Every cited label exists exactly once at a284420. Three of them are new at
a284420 and do not exist at 975feb3: `L:spatial-fourier-bound`,
`E:spatial-fourier-bound` and `E:damped-multiplier-comparison`. Every other
cited label exists exactly once, in the same file, at both revisions, and
every such cited lemma, proposition, theorem, equation and section has the
same statement and proof up to whitespace and braces, except
`P:spatial-smooth-ratio` (proof only), `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`
(statement and proof) and the section `S:spatial-occupation-foundation`
(the new lemma). TeX line numbers were moved to a284420 by a line map; each
moved range has the same text at both revisions, and the ranges inside the
two edited passages were mapped to the corresponding new passages by hand
(script checks recorded in `provenance/manuscript-anchor.json`).

## Scope

- The "What it states" column is a faithful paraphrase, sometimes
  shortened. The exact statement is the Lean type in
  `StratonovichHAMAudit/<Module>.lean` (step modules) or
  `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/<Module>.lean` (library modules: whole results, narrower results, foundations and proof steps);
  `Audit/<module>/` prints the elaborated types.
- The rows cover every public theorem (2050) and 418 definitions whose
  values are stated as facts or that name a manuscript object. The other 89
  public definitions have no rows of their own: 85 (for example `kappa`,
  `delta`, `gauge`, `counts`, `InventoryProduct.partialEval`,
  `OccupationPhysicalClass.volI`, `SpaceTimePositivity.timeMeasure`,
  `TerminalWick.chainMassReal`, `WaveGreenFourier.spherePhi` and
  `OccupationCeilingExact.stepG`) only name quantities or measures used in
  those statements, and four are the instances that make
  `TimeCompletion.Pre` a pre-inner-product space; read their bodies in the
  Lean source or in `Audit/`.
- The `StratonovichHAMAudit` modules check finite, algebraic and scalar
  steps only: exact identities, polynomial and rational certificates,
  real-power bookkeeping, parameter ranges, and a few finite-dimensional
  inner-product and finite-word facts. The exception is `HermiteWordFock`
  (wave L9), which applies `HermiteWord.cut_eq_raw` to the Fock model of
  `FockForm` and so formalizes the special case of `L:finite-word-cutoff`
  with one Gaussian coordinate per color (section "HermiteWordFock (narrower result: `L:finite-word-cutoff` for one Gaussian mode per color and single finite words; finite sums and Bochner integrals not formalized)"); the
  multi-mode case is not formalized.
- Section headings use three categories. (A) "whole result": every
  conclusion of the labelled result is a Lean conclusion under the
  manuscript's hypotheses, possibly with named supplied inputs that are
  disclosed (coverage class same-assumptions or inputs-supplied, conclusion
  full); no other section carries it. (B) "narrower result: ...": a labelled
  result some of whose conclusions are not Lean conclusions, or are proved
  for a modelled object (the class `O` by joint representatives, the rate in
  Rayleigh form, the cost in integral form, an abstract structure standing
  for an object the manuscript constructs, an object that is not constructed)
  whose identification with the manuscript's object is not formalized; the
  heading names what is missing. The one exception is a registered model
  choice (next item): a result whose only modelled object is such a choice
  stays a whole result, and its section names the model.
  Discharging a named input in a completion module does not turn a narrower
  result into a whole one. (C) "foundation: ..." or "proof steps ...": facts
  used by labelled results, not a labelled result themselves; every
  `StratonovichHAMAudit` section except `HermiteWordFock` is of this kind.
  The first cell of an Index row uses the same words.
- Model-choice register. A registered model choice is a documented
  definitional choice that is the standard construction of a manuscript
  object, recorded with the identification that is not formalized. M1 (wave
  L6, Le's decision 4): the wave Green measure in `d = 3` is
  `(s/(4 pi)) map (omega -> s omega) volume.toSphere`, Mathlib's sphere
  measure scaled to the radius-`s` sphere; its identification with the
  surface (Hausdorff or Riemannian) measure of the TeX is not proved. Results
  whose only modelled object is M1 (`L:low-alpha-convolution`,
  `L:phase-contractions`, and the sections `LowAlphaConvolution`,
  `PhaseContractions` and `L9Completed`) are whole results. Missing
  constructions are not model choices: they make a result narrower (for
  example the noise `W` of `P:masked-quotient-obstruction`, the ground
  family of `L:raw-block-indexed-cone`, the chain measures used for
  `L:uniform-series-tail`, the operator paths of `P:radius-mean-anchor`, the
  solution moments of `P:moment-growth-logconvex` and
  `C:static-moment-constant-continuity`).
- The seventy-six `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment` modules: 27 are whole-result
  modules (all with nothing supplied), 31 are narrower-result modules, and 18 are foundations or proof steps (`WaveKernel`,
  `SpectralHomog`, `TimeFractional`, `DampedNorms`, `GaussianIBP`,
  `GaussianTest`, `WeakSobolev`, `VariationalFloor`, `SeriesType`,
  `H1Density`, `FiniteWick`, `GaussianHermite`, `HermiteFock`, `WaveGreen`,
  `WaveGreenFourier`, `SpaceTimePositivity`, `IntervalScalar`,
  `StaticPhaseCauchy`). Some modules without a section of their own are
  covered in the section of the module they serve. Together they model
  `H:homog` and give, by labelled result, 25 whole results (with the
  manuscript's hypotheses alone; none remains whole with named inputs), 18
  narrower results with the manuscript's hypotheses, and steps or parts of
  30 further results
  (see `COMPLETION.md`), to the scopes specified below (the narrower
  conclusions are stated per result). Forty-seven (the 25 whole and 18
  narrower results with the manuscript's hypotheses, and
  `E:kappa` and `E:driver-parameters`, `E:masked-time-schur` and
  `R:gaussian-one-variance-test`) need no supplied input:
  `L:gaussian-scalar-powers` is stated with the manuscript's own hypotheses.
  `L:gram-scalar-algebra` and `L:tube-rayleigh-tail` are proved under weaker
  hypotheses (no completeness or `C_ij >= 0`; no `delta < 1`) and also
  stated exactly as the manuscript does by the wrappers
  `gram_scalar_algebra_paper` and `rayleigh_tail_paper`; the Rayleigh
  lemma's "In particular" application to another proposition is not
  formalized. `E:kappa` and `E:driver-parameters` are proved from the
  numerical part of `H:homog` (a generalization) and also restated under the
  full hypothesis `H:homog`, which `HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance` models
  clause by clause (covariance measure, spectral measure, evenness,
  temperedness, positive-definiteness, scaling, parameter ranges).
  `L:equilibrium-gamma-beta` and `L:temporal-equilibrium` are stated with
  the manuscript's own hypotheses (`gamma_beta_paper`,
  `temporal_equilibrium_paper`). The finite slice of `S:compact-gaussian`,
  `L:gaussian-trace-bounds`, `P:finite-gaussian-matrix` and
  `R:gaussian-one-variance-test`, is stated with the manuscript's hypotheses
  (independent standard Gaussians on an arbitrary probability space) on top
  of a finite Gaussian integration-by-parts foundation (`GaussianIBP`).

# Formalization scope

## The paper's argument and where Lean enters

The paper bounds and identifies the growth of `log E[u(t,x)²]` for the
Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model. The argument has three layers.

1. **Stochastic and analytic layer.** The chaos expansion, the two-chain
   pairing integrals, Wick pairings (beyond finite families of Gaussian
   values), Gaussian integration (beyond finitely many standard Gaussians),
   imported bounds,
   Laplace transforms and the variational asymptotics. **Not in Lean**,
   except a few slices: the Laplace transforms of the wave kernel and of
   the two-time kernel and the subordination formula (`ClockCopy` and its
   foundation modules), the Gaussian transform of the spectral measure
   (`MaskedSpectralGrowth`), the uniform scalar frequency row
   (`FrequencyRow`), the temporal completion `H_a` (`TimeCompletion`), the
   auxiliary mask norm (`MaskedAuxiliaryNorm`), the Gaussian heat envelope
   of the covariance (`VariationalMean`), a finite Hilbert-valued Bessel
   inequality (`PhaseBessel`), the wave Green measures `G_s` for
   `d = 1, 2, 3` (`WaveGreen`), the spectral identity and positive
   definiteness of `Gamma = delta_0(dx_1) dx_2` (`QuotientObstruction`), a
   finite Gaussian comparison under the positive semidefinite order
   (`GaussianComparison`), the two wave variance directions in spectral
   form (`WaveTwoVariances`), the variational floor and the Rayleigh-form
   rate (`VariationalFloor`, `VariationalRate`), the deterministic Fourier
   bound `L:spatial-fourier-bound` for the smooth spatial ratio and the
   static controls
   (`SpatialFourierBound`, `SpatialSmoothRatio`, `SpatialStaticControls`,
   `SpatialOccupationCompleted`), series types and the continuity of the
   growth types in the temporal exponent (`SeriesType`, `TypeContinuity`),
   the white-noise bound formulas and clock transforms
   (`WhiteRelativeWidth`, `WhiteClockLaplace`), the coefficient bound of
   the interval inventory product (`InventoryProduct`), an abstract `L^2`
   limit of a regularized series under a uniform scaled moment bound
   (`UniformSeriesTail`), the density of test functions in the
   weak-gradient `H^1` (`H1Density`), the physical four-linear extension
   and the spatial energy (`SpatialFourLinear`), the full physical
   occupation class (`OccupationPhysicalClass`; both completed in
   `SpatialOccupationL7Completed`), the scalar and Hilbert-space steps
   of the static interaction and interval coefficient bounds
   (`IntervalScalar`, `IntervalScalarCompleted`), the spectral-mass
   identity `R_Gamma(1) = R_alpha` (`SpectralMassIdentity`), Gaussian
   smoothing as a Fourier multiplier (`DampedMultiplier`), the positivity of
   the space-time occupation form, the deterministic occupation ceiling and
   the spatial bracket (`SpaceTimePositivity`, `OccupationCeilingFinite`,
   `SpatialBracket`, completed in `L8Completed`), the masked rates
   (`RemoveMask`), the finite Wick formula and the terminal-chain Wick
   formula with the chain measures given by their masses (`FiniteWick`,
   `TerminalWick`), an abstract compact Young baseline (`SymplecticFree`)
   and the Cauchy steps of the static phase orders (`StaticPhaseCauchy`),
   the Fourier transforms of the wave Green measures in `d = 1, 2, 3` and
   Archimedes' law for the sphere measure (`WaveGreenFourier`), the low-alpha
   convolution bound and the static contraction bounds
   (`LowAlphaConvolution`, `PhaseContractions`, completed in `L9Completed`),
   the exact occupation constant and ceiling (`RawOccupationEnergy`,
   `OccupationCeilingExact`), the normalized Hermite polynomials and the
   finite Gaussian Fock layer with values in a Hilbert factor
   (`GaussianHermite`, `HermiteFock`) and their consumers `L:fock-form`,
   `L:interval-contractions` and `E:occupied-multiplication` (`FockForm`),
   and the scalar and numerical-range steps of the complex phase bounds
   (`ComplexPhaseScalar`).
2. **Reductions to explicit inequalities.** At many points the analytic
   argument reduces to a finite statement: an exponent range, an exact
   rational or square-root inequality, a polynomial that must stay positive
   on a region, a determinant or matrix inverse, a count of coefficients in
   a finite word, or an integral comparison once integrability is known.
   **These are what Lean checks.**
3. **Assembly** of the main theorems from the layers above. **Not in Lean.**

So each module checks one reduction in layer 2. Its hypotheses state the
facts that layer 1 supplies (for example positivity of a parameter,
integrability of a function, or an inequality proved analytically in the
paper). Its conclusion is the fact that the paper then uses.

| Whole result, inputs supplied | none: the three results formerly here (`P:radius-mean-anchor`, `P:moment-growth-logconvex`, `C:static-moment-constant-continuity`) are proved for abstract objects whose construction is missing, so they are narrower results | — |
| Narrower result (ledger heading "narrower result: ...", naming what is missing) | 18 results with the manuscript's hypotheses and steps or parts of 30 further results; 31 modules and the audit file `HermiteWordFock`: 943 theorems, 199 definitions | Kernel-checked; some conclusion of the result is not a Lean conclusion. | Checked step fact (`StratonovichHAMAudit/`, except `HermiteWordFock`) | 82 theorems, 6 definitions | Kernel-checked; the ledger gives its paper label and outside inputs |
| of which helper lemmas (`internal`) | 847 theorems, 51 definitions | Kernel-checked; used inside one module |
| Other public definitions | 89 | Named quantities and measures used in the statements (85), and four instances on `TimeCompletion.Pre` |
| Negative controls | 68 | Wrong variants that Lean must reject |

Heading categories (the same three are used in the statement ledger and in
every first cell of its Index by label). The ledger Scope keeps the
model-choice register. M1, its only entry, is the `d = 3` wave Green measure
`(s/(4 pi)) map (omega -> s omega) volume.toSphere` (wave L6, decision 4);
its identification with the surface measure of the TeX is not proved. A
registered standard choice preserves whole status only when the result's
section names the model (as `LowAlphaConvolution`, `PhaseContractions` and
`L9Completed` do for M1); a missing construction (the noise `W`, an abstract
ground family, chain measures fixed by their masses, abstract random paths,
an abstract moment function) makes the result narrower.
(A) "whole result": every conclusion of the labelled result is a Lean
conclusion under the manuscript's hypotheses, possibly with named supplied
inputs that are disclosed (coverage class same-assumptions or
inputs-supplied, conclusion full; at present every whole result has the
manuscript's hypotheses alone); no other module carries it. (B) "narrower
result: ...": a labelled result some of whose conclusions are not Lean
conclusions, or are proved for a modelled object (such as the class `O` by
joint representatives, or the rate in Rayleigh form and the cost in integral
form) whose identification with the manuscript's object is not formalized;
the heading names what is missing. (C) "foundation: ..." or "proof steps of
...": facts used by labelled results, not a labelled result themselves; the
`StratonovichHAMAudit` step modules are all of this kind.

Modules are counted by their ledger heading; a module that also proves
pieces of other results is counted once. Completion modules
(`ClockCopyHomog`, `MaskedContinuousWaveCompleted`, `L9Completed`,
`SpatialOccupationCompleted`, `SpatialOccupationL7Completed`,
`IntervalScalarCompleted`, `L8Completed`) discharge named inputs of other
modules; discharging an input does not make a narrower result whole, so
`L8Completed` (narrower results, including `L:uniform-series-tail` with the
chain measures fixed only by their masses) and the spatial and occupation
modules remain "narrower result". `ClockCopyHomog`,
`MaskedContinuousWaveCompleted` and `TimeSchur`, which have no section of
their own, count as whole-result modules; `DampedNorms`, `SpectralHomog`,
`TimeFractional`, `WaveKernel`, `GaussianIBP`, `GaussianTest` and
`WeakSobolev` as foundations.

These counts describe the package. They are not a percentage of the paper.
The 25 whole results and 18 narrower results with the manuscript's
hypotheses are deterministic lemmas,
propositions and corollaries used inside the analytic argument, and the
occupation ceiling `T:intrinsic-occupation-ceiling` (a narrower result: both
forms with the exact constant, for `S_c^pos`; `C_2 <= U_2` not formalized);
the other three main theorems are not formalized.

## Reading a statement

For each declaration, check three things against the paper:

1. the hypotheses match what the paper has available at that point;
2. the conclusion is what the paper uses next;
3. parameter ranges, strict versus non-strict inequalities and quantifier
   order agree.

The [statement ledger](docs/statement-ledger.md) records this for every row.
`Audit/<module>/` prints the full elaborated types, so the statements can be
read without opening an editor.

## Not yet included

Three development modules use a Gaussian-chaos library that is not yet
public: normalized Gaussian coordinates, vector Gaussian projection and
colored vector words. They are checked in the private development record
and will be added here when that library is released.

## Possible next steps

- the finite pair-partition counts behind the two-chain integrals;
- a reusable Laplace-to-time growth lemma, with its analytic inputs as
  hypotheses;
- the constant and exponent algebra of the main upper and lower bounds.

   98| \begin{proposition}[The unmasked Rayleigh rate]
   99|   \label{P:variational-unmasked-rate}
  100|   On complex $L^2(\R^d)$, the operator $H_s = -\Delta-h_s$ is self-adjoint on
  101|   $H^2$, with form domain $H^1$ and form $q_s(f) = \|\nabla f\|_2^2-\int
  102|   h_s|f|^2$. Its spectral bottom $E_s$ is uniformly negative on $I$. The
  103|   positive rate $\lambda_{\Psi,s} = \sqrt{-E_s}$ satisfies
  104|   \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-real-rayleigh}
  105|     \lambda_{\Psi,s}^2
  106|     =\sup_{\substack{f\in H^1(\R^d;\R)\\\|f\|_2=1}}
  107|     \left(\int h_sf^2-\|\nabla f\|_2^2\right).
  108|   \end{equation}
  109|   It is Lipschitz on $I$, and $I_\Psi: = \int_0^1\lambda_{\Psi,s}\ud s$ is
  110|   positive and finite. No eigenstate at the unmasked bottom is asserted.
  111| \end{proposition}

   101	\begin{lemma}[Deterministic Fourier bound for the spatial energy]
   102	  \label{L:spatial-fourier-bound}

   113	\begin{proof}

   115	  and compact support forces $g=0$, contrary to $\|g\|_2=1$. Put $Q=g^2$ and
   116	  use the unnormalized Fourier transform
   117	  \[
   118	    \mathcal{F}_0Q(\xi)=\int_{\R^d}e^{-i\xi\cdot x}Q(x)\ud x.
   119	  \]

   121	  $c_d^{-1}\widehat Q$, with $c_d=(2\pi)^{-d/2}$.
   122	  The autocorrelation
   123	  \[
   124	    c_Q(y)=\int_{\R^d}Q(x)Q(x-y)\ud x

   127	  identity~\eqref{E:masked-spectral-convention} to this Schwartz function.
   128	  Its inner Fourier integral is $|\mathcal{F}_0Q(\xi)|^2$, since $Q$ is real.
   129	  Hence
   130	  \[
   131	    A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)=\int c_Q(y)\Gamma(\ud y)
   132	    =\int|\mathcal{F}_0Q(\xi)|^2\mu(\ud\xi).
   133	  \]

   135	  Radon, while $|\mathcal{F}_0Q|^2$ is Schwartz and $\mu$ is tempered.
   136	  No density of either measure is required.
   137	
   138	  Since $\|Q\|_1=1$, we have $|\mathcal{F}_0Q|\le1$. Integration by parts
   139	  and the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality give
   140	  \[
   141	    |\xi|\,|\mathcal{F}_0Q(\xi)|
   142	    \le\|\nabla Q\|_1
   143	    \le2\|g\|_2\|\nabla g\|_2=2\sqrt b.
   144	  \]

   146	  \[
   147	    |\mathcal{F}_0Q(\xi)|^2\le\frac{8b}{4b+|\xi|^2}.

   150	  Lemma~\ref{L:damped-homogeneous-norms}, together

   152	  \[

   154	    =q^{\alpha-2}R_\alpha<\infty.
   155	  \]

   157	  \[
   158	    A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)\le8b\mathcal{R}_\Gamma(2\sqrt b)
   159	    =2^{1+\alpha}R_\alpha b^{\alpha/2}.

   166	\begin{proposition}[The finite smooth spatial ratio]
   167	  \label{P:spatial-smooth-ratio}

   179	\begin{proof}

   181	  weak gradient would have Fourier transform supported only at zero, and hence
   182	  would vanish. Its square is nonnegative nonzero smooth compact, so the

   184	  Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-static-controls} gives

   190	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-dilation}
   191	    A_{\mathrm{sp}}(U_\ell g)=\ell^\alpha A,\qquad
   192	    b(U_\ell g)=\ell^2b(g).

   195	  $\ell^{-d}$ from $\ud x$, and $\ell^{\alpha-d}$ from the Radon pushforward.

   202	    \ell^2=uL^2/b,\qquad
   203	    \theta=(1+u)L^2/(\ell^\alpha A).

     2	\label{S:unmasked-variational}

     4	Fix a nonzero covariance satisfying Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}, including its
     5	original amplitude, and set $a = \alpha_0$. Define the full class
     6	\begin{equation}\label{E:variational-positive-class}

    14	$|z| < 1$ and zero otherwise, then $b(4s-2)\prod_{j=1}^db(x_j)$ belongs to this

    21	\subsection{Global bounds and the unmasked spectral bottom}
    22	
    23	\begin{lemma}[Gaussian envelope for the original covariance]
    24	  \label{L:variational-heat-envelope}
    25	  For the normalized heat kernel $p_\epsilon(x) =
    26	  (2\pi\epsilon)^{-d/2}e^{-|x|^2/(2\epsilon)}$,
    27	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-heat-envelope}
    28	    (\Gamma*p_\epsilon)(x)
    29	    =\int e^{i\xi\cdot x}e^{-\epsilon|\xi|^2/2}\mu(\ud\xi),
    30	    \qquad
    31	    0\le(\Gamma*p_\epsilon)(x)
    32	    \le(\Gamma*p_\epsilon)(0)<\infty.
    33	  \end{equation}
    34	  The value at zero is strictly positive.
    35	\end{lemma}
    36	
    37	\begin{proof}
    38	  A positive tempered Radon measure has polynomial ball growth. Indeed, evaluate
    39	  its tempered bound on a nonnegative smooth cutoff equal to one on $B_1$,
    40	  dilated by $R \ge 1$. Its finitely many Schwartz seminorms are bounded by
    41	  $CR^N$, so positivity gives a ball-mass bound $CR^N$. Summing dyadic annuli
    42	  shows that $(1+|x|)^{-L}$ is integrable for $L > N$. Apply this separately to
    43	  $\Gamma$ and $\mu$. Gaussian weights are therefore integrable against both
    44	  measures. The classical convolution on the left is finite and smooth locally
    45	  in $x$: on compact $x$ sets its translated Gaussian derivatives are bounded by
    46	  any fixed sufficiently fast polynomial weight in the integration variable.
    47	
    48	  Pair the convolution with a Schwartz test $\varphi$. Absolute Fubini is
    49	  justified by these weights. The resulting pairing is that of $\Gamma$ with
    50	  $p_\epsilon*\varphi$. Applying the spectral convention in
    51	  Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} and the identity $\int p_\epsilon(y)e^{-i\xi\cdot
    52	  y}\ud y = e^{-\epsilon|\xi|^2/2}$ gives exactly the right side
    53	  of~\eqref{E:variational-heat-envelope} as a distribution. The heat kernel is
    54	  even, so either Fourier sign gives that same Gaussian multiplier. Its spectral
    55	  integral is absolutely finite and continuous in $x$ by dominated convergence.
    56	  Thus, equality of the two continuous distributions gives equality at every
    57	  $x$, without an extra normalization factor. The physical convolution is
    58	  nonnegative. Evenness of $\mu$ makes the spectral integral real, and its
    59	  absolute value is bounded by its total Gaussian mass, the value at zero.
    60	  Finally, $\Gamma \ne 0$ and $p_\epsilon > 0$ give strict positivity there.
    61	  This proves Lemma~\ref{L:variational-heat-envelope}.
    62	\end{proof}
    63	
    64	\begin{lemma}[Global regularity of the original mean]
    65	  \label{L:variational-global-mean}
    66	  Every mixed time and space derivative of $h_s$ is globally bounded in space,
    67	  uniformly on compact time intervals. In particular, for $I = [0,1]$ there are
    68	  finite constants $M,C_\Psi$ such that
    69	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-global-mean}
    70	    0\le h_s(x)\le M,\qquad
    71	    \|h_s-h_t\|_\infty\le C_\Psi|s-t|,
    72	    \qquad s,t\in I.
    73	  \end{equation}
    74	\end{lemma}
    75	
    76	\begin{proof}
    77	  Extend $\Psi$ by zero in time; its compact support inside $(0,1)$ makes this a
    78	  smooth extension. For any mixed derivative $D\Psi$, a fixed $\epsilon > 0$ and
    79	  compactness of its common spatial support give $|D\Psi(t,x)| \le
    80	  C_Dp_\epsilon(x)$ for all $t,x$. Here the heat kernel has a positive minimum
    81	  on that support. Lemma~\ref{L:variational-heat-envelope} consequently bounds
    82	  $\Gamma*|D\Psi(t,\cdot)|$ uniformly in $t,x$. Ordinary local differentiation
    83	  against the Radon measure gives the corresponding derivatives of the
    84	  convolution. After the change $r = s-t$,
    85	  \[
    86	    h_s(x)=\int_\R |r|^{-a}
    87	    (\Gamma*\Psi(s-r,\cdot))(x)\ud r.
    88	  \]
    89	  For $s$ in a compact interval the relevant $r$ lie in a fixed bounded
    90	  interval. The preceding global bound times $|r|^{-a}$ is integrable since $a <
    91	  1$. Every derivative thus falls on the smooth test and passes through the
    92	  integral by dominated convergence, with the claimed global spatial bounds.
    93	  Nonnegativity follows from positive kernels. The bounded time derivative
    94	  proves the Lipschitz estimate. No directional decay of the mean has been
    95	  inferred. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:variational-global-mean}.
    96	\end{proof}

    98	\begin{proposition}[The unmasked Rayleigh rate]
    99	  \label{P:variational-unmasked-rate}
   100	  On complex $L^2(\R^d)$, the operator $H_s = -\Delta-h_s$ is self-adjoint on
   101	  $H^2$, with form domain $H^1$ and form $q_s(f) = \|\nabla f\|_2^2-\int
   102	  h_s|f|^2$. Its spectral bottom $E_s$ is uniformly negative on $I$. The
   103	  positive rate $\lambda_{\Psi,s} = \sqrt{-E_s}$ satisfies
   104	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-real-rayleigh}
   105	    \lambda_{\Psi,s}^2
   106	    =\sup_{\substack{f\in H^1(\R^d;\R)\\\|f\|_2=1}}
   107	    \left(\int h_sf^2-\|\nabla f\|_2^2\right).
   108	  \end{equation}
   109	  It is Lipschitz on $I$, and $I_\Psi: = \int_0^1\lambda_{\Psi,s}\ud s$ is
   110	  positive and finite. No eigenstate at the unmasked bottom is asserted.
   111	\end{proposition}
   112	
   113	\begin{proof}
   114	  The Fourier Laplacian $A = -\Delta$ is self-adjoint on $H^2$, being
   115	  multiplication by $|\xi|^2$ with its maximal domain. Multiplication $B_s =
   116	  -h_s$ is bounded self-adjoint with norm at most $M$. Thus, $H_s = A+B_s$ is
   117	  densely defined, symmetric and closed on $H^2$; the two graph norms are
   118	  equivalent under a bounded perturbation. For real $b > M$,
   119	  \[
   120	    H_s-ib=(I+B_s(A-ib)^{-1})(A-ib).
   121	  \]
   122	  The first factor has a Neumann inverse because $\|B_s(A-ib)^{-1}\| \le M/b <
   123	  1$, and the same holds with $+ib$. To check self-adjointness directly, for $u
   124	  \in D(H_s^*)$ solve $(H_s-ib)v = (H_s^*-ib)u$ with $v \in D(H_s)$. Then $u-v
   125	  \in \ker(H_s^*-ib) = \operatorname{Ran}(H_s+ib)^\perp = \{0\}$. Hence,
   126	  $D(H_s^*) = D(H_s)$.
   127	
   128	  Set $c_{\mathrm{shift}} = 1+M$ and $J_s = H_s+c_{\mathrm{shift}} \ge 1$.
   129	  Integration by parts on $H^2$ gives
   130	  \[
   131	    \|J_s^{1/2}f\|_2^2=q_s(f)+c_{\mathrm{shift}}\|f\|_2^2,\qquad
   132	    \|f\|_{H^1}^2\le\|J_s^{1/2}f\|_2^2
   133	    \le c_{\mathrm{shift}}\|f\|_{H^1}^2.
   134	  \]
   135	  Spectral cutoffs $1_{[1,n]}(J_s)$ show that $H^2 = D(J_s)$ is a core for the
   136	  half-power norm; Fourier cutoffs give its density in $H^1$. Completion in the
   137	  equivalent norms identifies $D(J_s^{1/2})$ and $H^1$ as $L^2$ subspaces, since
   138	  both norms dominate $L^2$. This proves the stated form domain.
   139	
   140	  The spectral lower bound gives one direction of the Rayleigh identity. For the
   141	  reverse, nonzero spectral projections in $[E_s,E_s+\epsilon]$ give unit $H^2$
   142	  vectors with Rayleigh values at most $E_s+\epsilon$. The bottom is finite
   143	  because the operator is bounded below and has finite Rayleigh tests. Let
   144	  $\epsilon\downarrow0$. Real tests give the same infimum: $q_s(u+iv) =
   145	  q_s(u)+q_s(v)$, so the quotient is the norm-weighted average of the nonzero
   146	  real quotients. This proves the Rayleigh identity with $-E_s$ on the left. The
   147	  following negative upper bound justifies writing that value as
   148	  $\lambda_{\Psi,s}^2$ in~\eqref{E:variational-real-rayleigh}.

   150	  Proposition~\ref{P:compact-original-common-trial} supplies, for this original
   151	  $\Psi$, one unit compactly supported $w$ and a finite plateau mask with a
   152	  common strictly negative upper bound $\epsilon_0 > 0$. Its trial has support
   153	  in $B_{2L}$; choose its plateau radius $R_0 \ge 2L$. The unmasked form on this
   154	  same $w$ is no larger. Consequently, $-M \le E_s \le -\epsilon_0 < 0$, and
   155	  $\sqrt{\epsilon_0} \le \lambda_{\Psi,s} \le \sqrt M$. Comparing identical unit
   156	  form tests gives $|E_s-E_t| \le \|h_s-h_t\|_\infty$ and therefore
   157	  \[
   158	    |\lambda_{\Psi,s}-\lambda_{\Psi,t}|
   159	    \le \frac{C_\Psi}{2\sqrt{\epsilon_0}}|s-t|.
   160	  \]
   161	  This also proves positivity and finiteness of $I_\Psi$. No compact-potential
   162	  spectral theorem was applied to $H_s$. This proves
   163	  Proposition~\ref{P:variational-unmasked-rate}.
   164	\end{proof}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Index-by-label category check (R5 replaced by the per-declaration rules R6-R12) (scratch tool, not part of the repo).
Usage: index_category_check.py WT [--verbose]
Rules:
 R1 the first parenthesized qualifier of every Index first cell starts with
    one of: "whole result", "narrower result", "foundation", "proof steps".
 R2 "whole result" needs the label's coverage row to be conclusion full, or
    (no coverage row and every module of the row is a whole-result section).
 R3 "narrower result" needs the label's coverage row not full (or no row), and
    some module of the row in a narrower-result section, unless the cell says
    "override".
 R4 a cell all of whose modules are foundation/proof-step sections may not say
    "whole result" or "narrower result" unless it says "override".
 R5 "nothing supplied" may not cover a theorem whose Lean binders take a named
    analytic input; "inputs supplied" may not cover a theorem whose binders take
    none, unless the cell names the declaration as input-free ("input-free").
"""
import re,sys,yaml,glob,os,collections
wt=sys.argv[1]; verbose='--verbose' in sys.argv
CATS=('whole result','narrower result','foundation','proof steps')
INPUTS=['GreenMass','GreenFourier','FockColumn','WaveFourierThree','ArchimedesLaw','H1TestDense','InventoryProduct',
 'SquarePairingBounds','SpaceTimeCS','RayleighFloor','OccupationCeilingK0','SquareBound','StaticControls','S1Bdd',
 'TerminalWickInput','RawBlockOriginalLower','TypeContinuityInputs','LeftYoungSumsConverge','FreeWaveData']
NAMED_BINDERS=['hmem','hnorm','hmod','hsm','hlink','hmeas','hcircle','hentire','hband','hgauss','hsplits','hfixed','hRB',
 'hborn','hmean','hY0','hY','hodd','hcoef','henergy','hZ0','hZ','hcol','hQ','hJ','hCPC','hCPF','hCPH','hJL2','hnormSG','hdense']
EXTRA={'ClockCopyHomog':'A','MaskedContinuousWaveCompleted':'A','TimeSchur':'A','DampedNorms':'C','SpectralHomog':'C',
 'TimeFractional':'C','WaveKernel':'C','GaussianIBP':'C','GaussianTest':'C','WeakSobolev':'C'}
led=open(wt+'/docs/statement-ledger.md').read().split('\n')
sec={}
for l in led:
    m=re.match(r'## (\w+) \((.*)\)$',l)
    if m:
        t=m.group(2)
        sec[m.group(1)]='A' if t.startswith('whole result') else 'B' if t.startswith('narrower') else 'C'
sec.update(EXTRA)
cov={}
for r in yaml.safe_load(open(wt+'/coverage.yaml'))['rows']:
    cov[r['paper']['label']]=r.get('conclusion') or ('full' if r['class']!='outside' else None)
claims={c['decl']:c for c in yaml.safe_load(open(wt+'/claims.yaml'))['claims']}
src={}
def sig(full):
    c=claims.get(full)
    if not c: return None,None
    f=wt+'/'+c['file']
    if f not in src: src[f]=open(f).read()
    short=full.split('.')[-1]
    m=re.search(r'^(?:@\[[^\]]*\]\s*)?(?:private\s+|protected\s+|noncomputable\s+)*(theorem|lemma|def|abbrev|structure|instance)\s+(?:[\w.]*\.)?'+re.escape(short)+r'\b(.*?)(?=:=|\bwhere\b|^\s*$)',src[f],re.M|re.S)
    if not m: return c['kind'],''
    return c['kind'],m.group(2)
def binders_inputs(s):
    hits=set()
    for n in INPUTS:
        if re.search(r'\(\s*[\w\']+(?:\s+[\w\']+)*\s*:\s*(?:[\w.]*\.)?'+n+r'\b',s): hits.add(n)
    for b in NAMED_BINDERS:
        if re.search(r'\(\s*'+b+r'\s*:',s): hits.add(b)
    return hits
i0=led.index('## Index by label'); i1=next(i for i in range(i0,len(led)) if led[i].startswith('Totals:'))
probs=[]; n=0
for k in range(i0,i1):
    l=led[k]
    if not l.startswith('| ') or l.startswith('| Paper label') or l.startswith('|---'): continue
    parts=re.split(r'(?<!\\)\|',l.strip()[1:-1]); c0=parts[0].strip(); c1=parts[1].strip()
    n+=1
    if c1.startswith('all declarations of'):
        if not re.match(r'no direct label \((foundation|proof steps)',c0): probs.append((k+1,'R1 aggregate row without category',c0[:90]))
        continue
    lm=re.match(r'(`[^`]+`|no direct label)\s*(.*)$',c0)
    lab=lm.group(1).strip('`'); rest=lm.group(2)
    q=re.match(r'\(([^()]*(?:\([^()]*\)[^()]*)*)',rest)
    qual=q.group(1) if q else ''
    cat=next((c for c in CATS if qual.startswith(c)),None)
    line=k+1
    if not cat: probs.append((line,'R1 no category',c0[:90])); continue
    decls=re.findall(r'`([\w.\']+)`',c1)
    mods=set()
    fulls=[]
    for d in decls:
        mod=d.split('.')[0]
        full=('StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.' if 'StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.'+d in claims else 'StratonovichHAMAudit.')+d
        fulls.append(full)
        mods.add('step' if full.startswith('StratonovichHAMAudit.') and mod!='HermiteWordFock' else sec.get(mod,'?'))
    row=cov.get(lab,'NOROW') if lab!='no direct label' else 'NOROW'
    over='override' in c0
    if cat=='whole result':
        ok=(row=='full') or (row=='NOROW' and mods<= {'A'})
        if not ok and not over: probs.append((line,'R2 whole result without full row/A section',c0[:90]))
    if cat=='narrower result' and not over:
        if row=='full' or not (mods & {'B'}) : probs.append((line,'R3 narrower result inconsistent (row %s, sections %s)'%(row,sorted(mods)),c0[:90]))
    if cat in ('whole result','narrower result') and mods and mods<= {'C','step'} and not over:
        probs.append((line,'R4 labelled-result category in foundation/proof-step section',c0[:90]))
# R6-R9: per-declaration homogeneity, via the per-declaration table
import subprocess,json as _json,os as _os
_t=_os.path.join(_os.path.dirname(_os.path.abspath(__file__)),'decltable.py')
_out='/tmp/_decltable_check.json' if False else _os.path.join(_os.path.dirname(_os.path.abspath(__file__)),'_decltable_check.json')
subprocess.run([sys.executable,_t,wt,_out],check=True,stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL)
_T=_json.load(open(_out))
_rows={r['line']:r for r in _T['rows']}
_by=collections.defaultdict(list)
for d in _T['decls']: _by[d['line']].append(d)
for line,ds in _by.items():
    cell=_rows[line]['cell']; cat=_rows[line]['category']
    kinds={d['kind'] for d in ds}; inps={tuple(d['inputs']) for d in ds}
    if len(kinds)>1: probs.append((line,'R6 row mixes definitions and theorems',cell[:80]))
    if len(inps)>1: probs.append((line,'R7 row mixes input sets %s'%sorted(inps),cell[:80]))
    if 'definition' in kinds and cat in ('whole result','narrower result'): probs.append((line,'R8 definitions in a whole/narrower row',cell[:80]))
    if cat in ('whole result','narrower result') and any(d['statement'] for d in ds) and any(not d['statement'] for d in ds if d['kind']=='theorem'):
        probs.append((line,'R9 wrapper and supporting/general theorems in one whole/narrower row',cell[:80]))
    for x in (sorted(inps)[0] if len(inps)==1 else ()):
        if not (('`'+x+'`' in cell) or re.search(r'\b'+re.escape(x)+r'\b',cell)): probs.append((line,'R10 qualifier does not name input %s'%x,cell[:80]))
    if len(inps)==1 and sorted(inps)[0] and 'nothing supplied' in cell.lower() and not re.search(r'named input|hypothes|kept|keeps|retain|supplied:|inputs? supplied',cell,re.I):
        probs.append((line,'R11 nothing supplied but inputs %s'%(sorted(inps)[0],),cell[:80]))
    if len(inps)==1 and not sorted(inps)[0] and re.search(r'inputs? supplied',cell,re.I) and not re.search(r'nothing supplied|input-free|no named analytic input|section',cell,re.I):
        probs.append((line,'R12 inputs supplied but no declaration takes a named input',cell[:80]))
import collections as _c
for p in probs: print('%d: %s | %s'%p)
print('cells checked: %d; problems: %d'%(n,len(probs)))
sys.exit(1 if probs else 0)

270	\begin{proposition}[Intrinsic variational lower bounds]
   271	  \label{P:variational-positive-scores}
   272	  For $c > 0$, the set of variational values
   273	  $\{cI_\Psi-v_\Psi/2:\Psi\in\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{pos}}\}$ is nonempty and
   274	  bounded above. Its finite real supremum $S_c^{\mathrm{pos}}$ is positive and
   275	  satisfies
   276	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-score-homogeneity}
   277	    S_c^{\mathrm{pos}}=c^{(4-\alpha)/(3-\alpha)}S_1^{\mathrm{pos}},
   278	    \qquad
   279	    Q_2\ge S_2^{\mathrm{pos}},
   280	  \end{equation}
   281	  where $Q_2$ is the original point liminf. The coefficient-one value is an
   282	  auxiliary variational value; no first-moment or source-constant identification
   283	  is asserted.
   284	\end{proposition}
   285	
   286	\begin{proof}
   287	  Write $k = 3-\alpha > 0$, $q = 4-\alpha = k+1$ and $m = q/k > 1$. Fix one
   288	  $\Psi_0$ from the nonempty class and put $I_0 = I_{\Psi_0} > 0$, $v_0 =
   289	  v_{\Psi_0} > 0$. Positivity of the latter is
   290	  Lemma~\ref{L:compact-raw-profile}. For $r_0 = (I_0/v_0)^{1/k} > 0$, which need
   291	  not be less than one, the exact real-power identity gives
   292	  \[
   293	    I_{D_{r_0}\Psi_0}-v_{D_{r_0}\Psi_0}/2
   294	    =r_0I_0-r_0^qv_0/2=r_0I_0/2>0.
   295	  \]
   296	  This positive value is obtained from a smooth nonnegative control.
   297	
   298	  For $c > 0$ put $r_c = c^{1/k}$ and $K_c = c^m > 0$.
   299	  Lemma~\ref{L:variational-control-dilation} and the exact scalar powers give,

   301	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-score-set-scaling}

  7238	  continuity of the power series on compact positive intervals gives $F(z) \le
  7239	  C_L e^{Lz^{1/\nu}}$ for all $z \ge 0$. For $k \ge 1$, the inequality $c_kz^k

368	\begin{proposition}[Both variance directions]\label{P:wave-two-variances}
   369	  There is a finite $C_T$, depending on the fixed model, mask,
   370	  $a,\alpha,\gamma,T$, but not on $R,I$ or the orthonormal family, such that for
   371	  every finite complex $E$-orthonormal Schwartz family $\{e_k\}$ and every
   372	  Schwartz phase $z$,
   373	  \begin{align}
   374	    \sum_k\E|\ell_R(I;e_k,z)|^2
   375	    &\le C_T h^{2-a}B_\alpha(h)\|z\|_{E_{s-\gamma}}^2,
   376	    \label{E:wave-input-variance}\\
   377	    \sum_k\E|\ell_R(I;z,e_k)|^2
   378	    &\le C_T h^{2-a}B_\alpha(h)\|z\|_{E_{s-\gamma}}^2.
   379	    \label{E:wave-output-variance}
   380	  \end{align}
   381	  For every $\beta$ in~\eqref{E:variance-beta-range}, either right side may be
   382	  replaced by $C_{T,\beta}h^{2\beta}\|z\|_{E_{s-\gamma}}^2$.
   383	\end{proposition}
   384	
   385	\begin{proof}
   386	  Each entry in~\eqref{E:variance-normalized-kernel} is a product of two
   387	  continuous wave factors times $(\langle\xi\rangle\langle\eta\rangle)^{-1/2}$,
   388	  with a possible minus sign. Lemma~\ref{L:masked-continuous-wave} therefore
   389	  gives
   390	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variance-kernel-time-bound}
   391	    \|1_I\mathcal{K}_{ij}(\cdot;\xi,\eta)\|_{H_a^{\mathbb{C}}}^2
   392	    \le A_T h^{2-a}\Phi_h(\xi,\eta),
   393	    \qquad A_T = C_1(a)(1+T)^4.
   394	  \end{equation}
   395	  The positive even Radon measure $\nu_R$ satisfies the growth bound
   396	  \eqref{E:variance-actual-growth-constant}. Thus, all hypotheses of
   397	  Proposition~\ref{P:frequency-row} hold, and
   398	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variance-actual-row-bound}
   399	    \int\Phi_h(\xi,\xi-\lambda)\nu_R(\ud\lambda)
   400	    \le K C_\nu B_\alpha(h)\langle\xi\rangle^{-2\gamma}.
   401	  \end{equation}
   402	  No nonnegative physical inverse covariance of $\nu_R$ is needed.
   403	
   404	  The kernels used in Lemma~\ref{L:phase-bessel} belong to its stated $L^2$
   405	  space for each fixed $\lambda$. Indeed, $|c_r(t)| \le 1$ and $|b_r(t)| \le
   406	  \sqrt{2}\max(1,T)$ on $[0,T]$, by the high- and low-frequency representations.
   407	  The kernels are continuous into $L^2(0,T)$ in their frequency variables, hence
   408	  into $H_a^{\mathbb{C}}$ by Schur. Separability gives strong measurability.
   409	  Multiplication by shifted Schwartz components of $U$ or $V$ then gives the
   410	  required $L^2$ integrability. Later $\lambda$ integrals are of nonnegative
   411	  functions; their finiteness follows from the estimates below.
   412	
   413	  First fix $V = Jz$ and let $U_k = Je_k$ be the input family.
   414	  In~\eqref{E:variance-normalized-covariance} set
   415	  \[
   416	    g_j^\lambda(\eta) = \sum_{i=1}^2
   417	    1_I\mathcal{K}_{ij}(\cdot;\eta+\lambda,\eta)
   418	    \overline{V_i(\eta+\lambda)}.
   419	  \]
   420	  Lemma~\ref{L:phase-bessel} and Cauchy--Schwarz over the two output components
   421	  give
   422	  \begin{align*}
   423	    \sum_j\|g_j^\lambda(\eta)\|_{H_a^{\mathbb{C}}}^2
   424	    &\le 2\sum_{i,j}|V_i(\eta+\lambda)|^2
   425	    \|1_I\mathcal{K}_{ij}(\cdot;\eta+\lambda,\eta)\|_{H_a^{\mathbb{C}}}^2\\
   426	    &\le 4A_T h^{2-a}\Phi_h(\eta+\lambda,\eta)
   427	    \sum_i|V_i(\eta+\lambda)|^2.
   428	  \end{align*}
   429	  Change variables $\xi = \eta+\lambda$ in the Lebesgue integral for each
   430	  $\lambda$, apply Tonelli and~\eqref{E:variance-actual-row-bound}, and use
   431	  $\|z\|_{E_{s-\gamma}} = \|\langle\xi\rangle^{-\gamma}Jz\|_2$. This
   432	  proves~\eqref{E:wave-input-variance} with $C_T = 4A_TKC_\nu$.
   433	
   434	  Next fix $U = Jz$ and let $V_k = Je_k$ be the output family. After $\eta =
   435	  \xi-\lambda$ in~\eqref{E:variance-normalized-covariance}, put
   436	  \[
   437	    f_i^\lambda(\xi) = \sum_{j=1}^2
   438	    1_I\mathcal{K}_{ij}(\cdot;\xi,\xi-\lambda)U_j(\xi-\lambda).
   439	  \]
   440	  Apply the conjugated version of Lemma~\ref{L:phase-bessel}. Cauchy--Schwarz
   441	  over the two input components bounds its right side by
   442	  \[
   443	    4A_T h^{2-a}\int\Phi_h(\xi,\xi-\lambda)
   444	    \sum_j|U_j(\xi-\lambda)|^2\ud\xi.
   445	  \]

   447	  $\int\Phi_h(\eta+\lambda,\eta)\nu_R(\ud\lambda)$. Reflect $\lambda$ using the
   448	  evenness of $\nu_R$ and then use symmetry of $\Phi_h$. This row becomes
   449	  $\int\Phi_h(\eta,\eta-\lambda)\nu_R(\ud\lambda)$, which is bounded
   450	  by~\eqref{E:variance-actual-row-bound} with $\xi = \eta$. This proves
   451	  \eqref{E:wave-output-variance} with the same $C_T$.
   452	
   453	  Use Corollary~\ref{C:frequency-time} for $h^{2-a}$ times the row integral at
   454	  the two applications above to obtain the asserted $h^{2\beta}$ bounds,
   455	  including strict absorption of the critical logarithm. The constants are
   456	  uniform in $R,I$ and family size. The $R$-dependent admission estimate was not
   457	  used as this uniform variance bound. This proves
   458	  Proposition~\ref{P:wave-two-variances}.
   459	\end{proof}

    88	\begin{proposition}[Auxiliary mask norm]\label{P:masked-auxiliary-norm}
    89	  The measure $\nu_R$ is even, tempered and Radon, with
    90	  \begin{equation}\label{E:masked-auxiliary-growth}
    91	    \nu_R(B(y,r)) \le c_d^2L^2C_\Gamma r^\alpha
    92	  \end{equation}
    93	  for all $y \in \R^d$ and $r > 0$, uniformly in $R > 0$. If $H$ is a separable
    94	  complex Hilbert space and $F$ is an $H$-valued Schwartz function, then
    95	  \begin{equation}\label{E:masked-hilbert-fourier}
    96	    \int \|\widehat{\zeta_RF}(\xi)\|_H^2\mu(\ud\xi)
    97	    \le \int \|\widehat{F}(\eta)\|_H^2\nu_R(\ud\eta).
    98	  \end{equation}
    99	  For a real $H$, the same assertion holds after complexification.
   100	\end{proposition}
   101	
   102	\begin{proof}
   103	  Schwartz decay of $k_R$ and polynomial growth of $\mu$ show that
   104	  $\rho_R(\eta)$ is finite at every $\eta$. On compact sets of $\eta$, the
   105	  integrands have a common integrable bound. Dominated convergence therefore
   106	  makes $\rho_R$ continuous, and $\nu_R$ is Radon. Since $\zeta$ is real,
   107	  $k_R(-u) = \overline{k_R(u)}$. Evenness of $\mu$ gives evenness of $\rho_R$.
   108	  Tonelli's theorem gives
   109	  \[
   110	    \nu_R(B(y,r)) = c_d^2L\int |k_R(u)|\mu(B(y+u,r))\ud u.
   111	  \]
   112	  Proposition~\ref{P:masked-spectral-growth} and $\|k_R\|_1 = L$ give
   113	  \eqref{E:masked-auxiliary-growth}. Polynomial growth on centered balls proves
   114	  temperedness by the same dyadic argument as above.
   115	
   116	  Bochner Fourier integration gives
   117	  \[
   118	    \widehat{\zeta_RF}(\xi)
   119	    = c_d\int k_R(\xi-\eta)\widehat{F}(\eta)\ud\eta.
   120	  \]

   122	  integrability. It follows next for finite-rank Hilbert-valued functions. For
   123	  general $F$, take projections onto the successive spans of a countable
   124	  orthonormal basis of its separable range closure. They converge pointwise in
   125	  norm. The Schwartz bounds on $F$ dominate the Fourier integrals, proving the
   126	  identity by dominated convergence. In a finite-dimensional space the full
   127	  identity projection suffices; the zero space is immediate. The triangle
   128	  inequality and weighted Cauchy--Schwarz yield
